caption:
Indian Railways just commissioned its most advanced anti-collision system yet. It applies the brakes automatically - before a human even reacts.

On September 23, 2026, Indian Railways commissioned KAVACH 4.0 for the first time, deployed over 108 route kilometres on South Central Railway's Malkajgiri-Kamareddi section. KAVACH assists loco pilots in maintaining speed limits and automatically applies brakes when needed, built to Safety Integrity Level-4, the highest safety certification standard - preventing signal-passing-at-danger incidents and reducing collision risk. This upgrade builds on lessons from KAVACH 3.2, already running across 1,465 route kilometres on the same railway zone.

A signal missed used to mean a disaster. Now the train itself catches the mistake first.

Sources: Business Standard, Deccan Chronicle (2026)
